finding.shortLabel: Candidate landscape: 45 eliminated, 5 unlikely, Candidate B the sole survivor; probability model external-canonical

sources.locator: p. 158, John Gurney entry, bracketed documentary basis [WJ 2:422; MBCR 1:331; NEHGR 62:94; SPR Case #338; Weymouth Hist 3:251; TAG 10:70-73]
May 2026 supplementary same-name sweep; twelve Gurney surname variants across eighteen English parish, burial, probate, and licence collections
Thirteen PCC probate items 1577–1682; seven fix distinct John Gurneys living in England after 1637

finding.statement: Applying the shared matching-criteria profile and elimination scaffold across the full record sweep reduces the field to one surviving named candidate. Of 51 documented same-name English John Gurney households surfaced by the sweeps, three principal alternatives (Candidates A, C, and D) and 45 further households in the same-name clearance sweep are eliminated on structural grounds, and five single-attestation households are held at a low residual rather than eliminated outright. The 1636 Newgate apprentice, already de-conflated from the Braintree emigrant elsewhere in this graph on family-status and chronology grounds, carries no weight in the distribution. Candidate B is the only candidate the profile does not eliminate. The household-by-household enumeration of the cleared field is published in the identity case file at §8 and §8.6, cross-referenced as the master list rather than replicated here; the case file's own probability assessment for Candidate B, including its residual unknown-corridor estimate, is its own argument-specific synthesis and is likewise held external-canonical.
